summary: ADR-015 amends ADR-012 to permit one brokered macros.preview call from a user-invoked, manifest-declared command. Each request requires fresh host confirmation; the bounded sample and explicit value context are shown without evaluation, then the existing closed-world evaluator runs once with read-only state and regex disabled. The handler has no persistence, provider, nested broker or host-service access. Broker-path, static Pages Browser and real QuickJS/TUI Terminal evidence cover the narrow caller on those hosts; packaged WebView behavior and broader runtime or release readiness remain unverified.

sections.title: Amendment to ADR-012 Decision 4
sections.summary: The amendment admits a fifth caller for the existing macro interpreter: an explicitly invoked manifest command calling macros.preview through the broker. The host reviews the bounded sample and supplied values before execution, and the handler evaluates only after approval, once, with read-only mode and regex disabled. It returns bounded rendered text and sanitized diagnostics without persisting state or invoking another capability.

sections.title: Acceptance evidence and limits
sections.summary: Independent review accepted the narrow boundary. A broker-path test proves event activation is rejected, denial invokes the evaluator zero times, and approval invokes it once. The Desktop broker path, static Pages Browser probe and Terminal QuickJS/TUI path have been exercised. Those checks do not establish packaged WebView behavior, general host parity, package release readiness or completion of the extension runtime plan.
